photos_research.source: scripts/gmaps_detail.js and gmaps_detail2.js against the exact verified Maps URL, plus a third custom scrape scoped strictly to the DOM container with aria-label 'Photos of Taylor & Sons Roofing & Construction' (to rule out sidebar/other-business contamination).
photos_research.finding: The business's own Google photo gallery contains exactly 10 unique images (confirmed scoped to the business's own container, not a nearby/sidebar carousel). Visually inspected all 10 (see assets/raw/gm-*.jpg, downloaded then reviewed one by one): only 1-2 are even plausibly a Florida roofing jobsite (a close-up shingle/chimney shot with palm trees, and an ambiguous close-up of a worker drilling near a chimney with no distinguishing geography). The other 7-8 are clearly NOT this business's own Miami work: a California hillside estate with a tennis court, pool and ocean view; a Spanish-tile roof on a hillside home overlooking mountains and the ocean; a Colorado-style suburb in full autumn foliage with snow-capped peaks visible; another mountain-backdrop reroof in progress; a backyard with a wooden gazebo and chaparral hillside (West Coast, not flat Miami); a modern home with dry brush hillside in the background; a suburban street with distant mountains; and one completely unrelated interior bathroom vanity photo carrying a third-party watermark ('CRISNFT'), with no roofing content at all. A third-party directory mirror (bestsidingrepair.pages.dev) that lists the same business (same rating/phone/address) confirms it has NO photos of this business either, and its 'services' text is explicitly AI-generated ('Summarized by ChatGPT') boilerplate, not verified fact, so it was not used for content.
photos_research.conclusion: This Google Business Profile's photo set does not document this company's own work in Miami: it reads as a generic/shared marketing photo pack (a known practice among some roofing lead-gen vendors) mixed with at least one entirely unrelated photo. Usable, verifiably-this-business real photos: 0-2, below the 5-photo minimum. No Instagram or Facebook account could be found to source alternative real photos.
